prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP Manifesto 2015 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core stance
- Leave the EU via an early referendum; prefer Article 50 with a two‑year, orderly exit. Seek a UK–EU free trade deal, resume an independent WTO seat, and expand global trade. Restore UK legal and tax sovereignty.
- Rebalance power from elites to voters: citizen‑initiated referendums, real recall of MPs, open primaries, proportional voting with constituency link, tighter franchise (British citizens), stricter postal voting.

Fiscal plan and tax
- Stick to deficit elimination without raising taxes or cutting vital services. Fund commitments by:
  - Saving net £9bn by leaving the EU; cutting overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI; scrapping HS2; replacing the Barnett Formula; cutting government/QUANGO costs.
- Tax changes: raise personal allowance to at least £13,000 (no income tax on minimum wage); new 30% band (between £43.5k–£55k); 40% threshold to £55k; scrap inheritance tax; raise transferable allowance for married/civil partners to £1,500. Clamp down on multinational tax avoidance; restore UK tax sovereignty.

Immigration and borders
- Take back control from the EU. Australian‑style points system; five‑year moratorium on unskilled migration; cap high‑skill work visas at 50,000 p.a.; +2,500 Border Agency staff; count in/out system.
- Five years of tax/NI before access to most benefits and non‑urgent NHS. No amnesty for illegal immigrants; swift deportation of foreign criminals. Existing EU residents at referendum can stay.

NHS and social care
- Extra c. £12bn over five years; focus on frontline care. Recruit 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GPs in A&E pilots; abolish hospital parking charges; “Licence to Manage” for senior managers; local professional health boards.
- Curb health tourism (require insurance). End PFI use; oppose TTIP coverage of the NHS; scrap EU Working Time and Clinical Trials constraints.
- Increase social care funding (restore towards 2010 levels); integrate health and social care; dignity code; end 15‑minute visits; better deal for home‑care workers.

Welfare, pensions and families
- Lower benefit cap; tackle fraud; end ATOS‑style assessments (use GPs/specialists); protect disabled support; scrap bedroom tax; maintain HB for under‑25s; bolster foodbanks with funded advisers.
- Carers’ Allowance +£572/year. Flexible state pension window; stronger pensions guidance; ban cold‑calling. War widows’ pensions for life (retrospective).
- Childcare reform: deregulate to expand places and cut costs; wrap‑around school care 8am–6pm; emergency childcare registers; faster fostering/adoption; shared parenting presumption.

Education and skills
- Abolish KS1 SATs; reduce teacher workload/class sizes; support grammar schools (with later transfer options) and strong vocational/technical routes; apprenticeships can replace four non‑core GCSEs; first‑aid in PSHE.
- Scrap AS as stepping stone; streamline Ofsted; protect SEN and special schools.
- Waive tuition fees for UK students on STEMM/medicine degrees who work and pay tax in the UK for 5 years.

Housing and environment
- “Brownfield first”: national register, remediation support, stamp duty relief on first sale up to £250k; bring empty homes back; tighten planning to protect green belt; local referendums on major schemes. Prioritise locals for social housing; five‑year tax/NI rule for access. Tackle homelessness with a National Register. Support smaller rural developments; no mansion tax; inheritable mortgages.

Energy and transport
- Repeal Climate Change Act; end new wind/solar subsidies; back coal, nuclear, gas and shale (with a Sovereign Wealth Fund); scrap green levies/ETS to cut bills.
- Scrap HS2; consider re‑opening Manston; limit speed cameras to safety use; oppose road pricing/eCall; remove tolls where possible; scrap DCPC for HGVs.

Jobs and business
- Prioritise British workers; enforce minimum wage; curb abuse of zero‑hours (notice, no exclusivity, route to secure contracts). Reduce EU‑driven red tape. 20% business rates relief up to £50k RV; tackle late payments with HMRC‑backed sanctions; improve access to trade credit insurance. Free parking periods to revive high streets.

Farming, fishing, heritage, culture
- New Single Farm Payment (capped), support small/family farms; fairer supply chains; animal welfare tougher; clear food labelling.
- Exit CFP; 200‑mile UK EEZ; rebuild under‑10m fleet; science‑based conservation; support sea angling.
- Minister for Heritage and Tourism; remove VAT on listed building repairs; “Seaside Town Status”; save the pub (micro‑brewery relief; optional smoking rooms; oppose minimum pricing). Promote British values, integration and free speech.

Crime, justice and defence
- +3,500 frontline police/prison staff; +2,500 Border staff. Leave ECHR; UK Bill of Rights; scrap European Arrest Warrant. Tough on trafficking, grooming, FGM, forced marriage. Decriminalise TV licence non‑payment.
- Maintain/expand prison capacity; deport foreign prisoners; no prisoner votes.
- Defence: meet/exceed 2% GDP, +£4bn by 2020; retain Trident; rebuild capabilities and carriers; oppose EU army; no income tax while on active overseas service; create Director of National Intelligence.

Overseas aid
- Cut to 0.2% of GNI; focus on emergency relief, health, vaccinations, water/sanitation; merge DFID into FCO; “trade not aid.”
